title: Summary khipus
text: In the 2023 data no khipu records the group totals or column sums of another beyond chance (384 pairs against 415.6 on the offset baseline). The KFG release of October 2026 adds one exception, KH0697, which holds the section totals of AS109 (see the findings).

title: Compilations
text: Apart from the Basel fragments, no khipu combines runs from two or more other khipus.

title: Colonial documents
text: About 2,300 numbers from roughly 70 open transcriptions match no digitized khipu.

title: Huacones-Vilcahuasi hierarchy
text: Totals of one khipu on the next are at the level of chance (offset baseline).

title: Opposite attachment in copies
text: Recto on one copy and verso on the other in 7 of 10 pairs, against 50% at random (p ≈ 0.17).

title: Same suppliers in the same order
text: Deposit sizes of different Inkawasi khipus do not correlate by position.

title: Copies respect group boundaries
text: Run endpoints fall on group boundaries in 38% of cases against 46% expected.

title: Broken cords as lower bounds
text: Sums with a broken part are exact half as often (35% vs 68%), but the sign shows no loss of knots.

title: Equal-share convention
text: Pairs of equal-total groups are not over-represented corpus-wide (p ≈ 0.1).

title: Pachacamac style vs Huacho style
text: Simple numeric features do not separate site-museum Pachacamac khipus from Huacho khipus.

title: Sign convention
text: Neither attachment side nor colour marks negative cords.

title: Syllables in non-decimal khipus
text: The non-decimal signs of Wari-style khipus have far too small an alphabet for syllables.

title: Calendar reading
text: Group and cord counts give no calendar numbers beyond chance.

title: Colour of the product
text: Colour is not carried into copies and does not mark the product at Inkawasi.

title: Ordered totals and strided copies
text: Group totals of one khipu repeated in the same order on another (192 khipus with at least three non-round totals ≥ 100): every pair above the shifted-value baseline is a copy already known or a second recording of one object. Within Inkawasi, every p-th record of one khipu laid against consecutive records of another (strides 2–8): only UR269 ~ UR275 stands out; the rest is at the level expected from the number of strides and offsets tried.

title: Place-dependent constants and small-valued copies
text: A value fixed by the place of the record in its block, as on UR269, was sought on every khipu and every cord position (blocks between separator groups; records shuffled within blocks): UR269 is the only clear case (p ≈ 0.003; next UR037, p ≈ 0.05 on values of 2 and 4). Identical groups of six or more small values (< 100) on khipus with different museum numbers: every rare match is a second recording of one object or AS003 ~ AS215; the rest are uniform runs such as seven 10s.

title: A hidden network
text: Every pair of the 757 khipus (286,146 pairs) was scored for shared rare values (≥ 100, not multiples of 10) and for a group total of one standing on a cord of the other. Beyond the known links, second recordings of one object under two numbers and one new link (AS104 ~ UR234), the excess over shifted values is spread thinly over thousands of pairs, and khipus from one place share no more rare values than random khipus of the same size (place labels shuffled: p = 0.075). The known links are small separate groups, not parts of one structure.

title: Knot direction and attachment side in copies
text: On cords that two linked khipus share, the copy does not follow the original's knot direction beyond what khipus of the same place share anyway (long knots are reversed on about half of the copies), nor its attachment side (recto or verso of a whole khipu follows how bundles were laid out: both members of a two-khipu bundle are always opposite). Colour is kept more often than chance (26% against 16%). Cords attached on the other side within a khipu mark sections — whole groups at the start or end, knotless separators — and are not copied.

title: Operations beyond addition
text: Fractions (one group equal to another times p/q with rounding, q = 2–12), products (a × b = c within a group), squares and cubes, and a circle's area (π·r² or 3·r²) were sought in every khipu. Against values shifted by 1–5, with each value combination counted once and round numbers left out: fractions 7 against 11.9, products 228 against 217, powers 167 against 142, circle 188 against 245 — none above chance. Besides sums, only whole-number multiples (×8 on UR271, halving on AS026B) and proportional shares (the Berlin ninths) occur.

title: Breakdown tables outside Inkawasi
text: Group totals of one khipu that reappear, in order, as the first cords of another khipu's groups (the Inkawasi nine-part tables) were sought in the whole corpus: pairs with four or more such totals number 4 against 0.5 with shifted values, and all four are Inkawasi pairs already known. Outside Inkawasi nothing stands above the baseline.

title: Colour of total cords
text: A cord equal to the sum of the others in its group has a colour of its own more often than chance (56 of 134 against 39), but the excess comes from the Inkawasi peanut ledgers (white gross cords) and UR297; elsewhere 16 of 50 against 13.2 (p = 0.16). Marking the total by colour is a local habit, not a general rule.

title: Formats and find-places
text: Khipus that repeat the same unit of group sizes (for example six cords and a separator) come from the same place no more often than chance (19% of pairs against 11%, p = 0.20; 22 khipus with a known place). Column profiles that look alike point to the same place only weakly (20% against 8%, p = 0.06), although they do find second recordings and known links.
